title: The Unexpected Orchard
premise: Emrys Iversen, a pastry chef drowning in debt and guarding her heart behind the counter of her failing café, agrees to pose as the girlfriend of Wren Calloway at his family's reunion — held, inconveniently, at the abandoned orchard where he grew up and where his late mother's legacy is being sold out from under him. What begins as a transactional lie deepens as Emrys uncovers the truth: Wren's uncle is fraudulently seizing the orchard through forged debts, and the proof may be buried in his mother's old recipe journals. As Emrys bakes her way into the family's memory — recreating lost recipes from those journals — she must choose between protecting her own fragile finances and fighting for a man who was only supposed to be pretend. The climax comes at the orchard's auction, where Emrys exposes the forgery using a recipe journal's handwriting evidence and her own testimony, saving the orchard but nearly losing Wren when he learns how much she hid. In the end, they rebuild together: the café survives on a new partnership, the orchard reopens as a community harvest space, and Emrys finally lets love move from past tense to present.
about_author: Felix Underhill is the pen name of a former line cook turned novelist who writes love stories set in kitchens, markets, and other places where people feed each other what they can't say aloud. They live near an overgrown apple orchard that inspired this book.

chapters.title: Three Missed Payments
chapters.summary: Emrys Iversen's POV. Emrys opens her struggling café, fields a final notice from the bank, and turns down a flirtatious regular named Wren with practiced deflection. The beat is weary self-protection: she has learned that letting things in means losing them.

chapters.title: The Regular Who Lingers
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren admits to himself why he keeps coming back every morning, then confesses his problem to Emrys: his family reunion is in two weeks and he needs a date to survive it. She laughs him off; he leaves his number anyway. Beat: hopeful vulnerability meeting a closed door.

chapters.title: Terms and Conditions
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. A second foreclosure warning arrives, and Wren returns with an offer: paid companionship for one weekend, cash up front. Desperate, she negotiates rules — no real names in front of family, no touching after dessert, no falling for anyone. Beat: a deal struck on shaky ground.

chapters.title: The Orchard Road
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. They drive to Hollowmere Orchard, Wren narrating memories of his mother's cider press and the summer everything ended. Emrys watches him soften and realizes the fake girlfriend role requires more acting than expected. Beat: the past pressing close.

chapters.title: Reunion of Strangers
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Emrys meets the sprawling Calloway clan, including the smooth-talking Uncle Aldous, who controls the estate. She improvises convincingly until Wren's grandmother asks about 'the recipe Emrys brought' — a detail Wren never mentioned. Beat: comedy shading into unease.

chapters.title: What Grandmother Kept
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Grandmother Ida privately tells Wren she suspects Aldous forged his late sister's debts to force the orchard's sale, and that her daughter's recipe journals might prove it. Wren, rattled, says nothing to Emrys. Beat: a secret that will cost him.

chapters.title: Cider and Confessions
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. By the bonfire, slightly drunk on fresh cider, Emrys and Wren trade almost-truths about grief — her broken engagement, his mother. The fake-date boundary blurs when he tucks her blanket closer. Beat: intimacy arriving ahead of schedule.

chapters.title: The Locked Study
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren sneaks into Aldous's study hunting the deed papers and finds a locked drawer and a lawyer's card. He's nearly caught by Aldous himself, who offers him money to stop asking questions. Beat: the antagonist shows his teeth.

chapters.title: Dessert Is Served
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Emrys wins the family over by baking her signature tart with orchard apples, and Ida embraces her like a granddaughter. Watching Wren watch her, Emrys breaks her own rule one heartbeat too long. Beat: the fake becomes dangerously real by dessert.

chapters.title: Last Train Home
chapters.summary: Both POVs alternate. The weekend ends; at the station, neither wants to say goodbye. Emrys boards, then gets off at the last second, telling herself it's about the recipe journals she now wants to help find. Beat: choosing to stay past the point of safety.

chapters.title: Journals and Jitters
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Back home, Emrys balances bank threats with secret research into property law, while Wren mails her photocopies of his mother's journals. Their letters grow less about evidence and more about each other. Beat: longing conducted through paper.

chapters.title: The Forged Hand
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Comparing signatures in the journals against the loan documents, Wren confirms the forgery — but a lawyer warns that without the original documents or a witness, it's unwinnable before the auction date. Beat: hope sharpened into urgency.

chapters.title: Aldous Comes Calling
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Aldous appears at Emrys's café, having discovered her role is fabricated, and offers to pay off her mortgage if she disappears from Wren's life. She refuses — then finds her café's lease mysteriously terminated. Beat: blackmail tightens the screws.

chapters.title: The Fight in the Kitchen
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren learns Emrys was approached and hid it from him; feeling betrayed and protective, they fight bitterly in the café kitchen. He accuses her of treating everything as a transaction; she throws his secrecy back at him. Beat: the midpoint rupture.

chapters.title: Empty Counter
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Alone, Emrys packs up the café and confronts the pattern: she ends things before they end her. Ida visits unexpectedly, sees through her, and shares how Wren's mother regretted the loves she let leave. Beat: the mirror moment.

chapters.title: The Missing Page
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Rereading his mother's journals in grief, Wren discovers a torn page referenced but missing — and realizes Emrys unknowingly has it: she used the journal page as packing paper for the tarts she shipped him weeks ago. Beat: the key hidden in plain sight.

chapters.title: Everything He Didn't Say
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Wren arrives at her shuttered café, finds her boxing up her life, and apologizes first. He asks not for forgiveness but for partnership. Emrys hands him the torn page she kept because it felt like a promise. Beat: reconciliation built on honesty.

chapters.title: Auction Day
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. At the Hollowmere auction, Aldous's lawyer presents the sale; Wren presents the journal, the torn page matching the forged ledger, and Ida's sworn testimony. Bidding halts as the auctioneer demands verification. Beat: the climax ignites.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. When Aldous claims Emrys is a hired actress discrediting the family, Emrys takes the floor and testifies to his bribery attempt — risking her credibility and naming her own desperation aloud. The crowd of neighbors corroborates. Beat: justice outside the law, spoken publicly.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Apples
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The auction collapses; police open an investigation into Aldous, and the orchard passes to Ida, who immediately deputizes Wren and Emrys to restore it. Exhausted, they walk the rows of trees at dusk, hands finally, officially intertwined. Beat: exhale and beginning.

chapters.title: Rising Dough
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Spring: the café reopens as 'Iversen & Calloway,' stocked with orchard fruit, its first payment made on time. Emrys hangs a new rule above the counter — no keeping score. Beat: belonging chosen daily, not granted once.

chapters.title: The Unexpected Orchard
chapters.summary: Both POVs converge. At the orchard's reopening festival, Wren proposes under the oldest apple tree with a ring baked inside a tart — her own trick turned back on her. Emrys says yes before he finishes asking. Final beat: love, present tense, rooted and ripening.
